name: Low Earth Orbit, 400 km
notes: Cheapest to reach. Atmospheric drag demands constant station-keeping, which shortens mission life.

name: Sun-Synchronous Orbit, 705 km
notes: Crosses the equator at the same local solar time every pass, so lighting is consistent. The Landsat orbit.

name: Geostationary Transfer Orbit
notes: Passes through the Van Allen belts twice per orbit. High radiation dose degrades solar arrays faster.

name: Geostationary Orbit, 35,786 km
notes: Fixed above one point on Earth. Continuous downlink, almost no eclipse, but expensive to reach.

name: Low Lunar Orbit, 100 km
notes: Lunar mascons perturb the orbit, so station-keeping is constant. Relies on the Deep Space Network.

name: Mars Areocentric Orbit
notes: At 1.524 AU the Sun gives 586 W/m2, only 43% of what an array collects at Earth. Insertion assumes aerobraking, as Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter used, which trades months of time for a much smaller burn.
